subject: Post-demo: SLA comparison & proposed failover qualification for MediCore
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom Barton <tom.barton@medicore.com>, Ava Clinical <ava@medicore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:10:00 -0000
Subject: Post-demo: SLA comparison & proposed failover qualification for MediCore

Hi Tom / Ava —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and a proposed set of next steps so we can validate the reliability behaviors you care about (latency SLOs, rate limits, error budgets, and failover semantics). We want to make sure MediCore has concrete evidence showing how Redwood compares to the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned.

Recap (what we covered):
- Baseline latency and throughput for the targeted model family (50–512 token requests)
- Rate-limit behavior under burst traffic and steady-state sustained throughput
- Failover model: regional fallback + smaller-variant degrade path vs. hard 503s
- Audit/telemetry: token-level traces, error budgets, and per-route SLIs in the Console

Proposed qualification tests (high level):
1) Synthetic peak window (2h): ramp to sustained 600 rps, measure p50/p95/p99, observed error-rate.
2) Graceful degradation test: simulate capacity pressure and verify automatic fallback to a smaller-quantized model (compare response deltas and regeneration latency).
3) Cross-region failover: terminate primary availability zone and validate request routing to fallback region (target mean RTO < 2s added).
4) Rate-limit enforcement: run concurrent clients to map limit thresholds and consistent 429 behavior + Retry-After semantics.
5) Cold-start/kv-cache warm-up: measure first-request penalty and token-cost delta over 30-minute windows.

I've attached a short SLA comparison matrix and a draft PoC test plan that maps each test to expected pass/fail criteria. If you want, Ben and I can own the test execution; we'll need a brief environment window and service account creds for the PoC.

Next concrete asks from MediCore:
- Confirm a 2-hour window availability next week (we suggested Wed/Thu mornings PT)
- Provide an example production workload spec (qps, avg tokens, peak percentiles)
- Share any compliance evidence needs beyond SOC 2 (we saw your PDF request attached and will respond in the next message)

I'll also copy Marcus to flag the outbound marketplace questions and any enterprise-level SLA exceptions.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim | Enterprise Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sla-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), proposed-poctest-plan.md (markdown), medicore-soc2-request.pdf (pdf)

From: Tom Barton <tom.barton@medicore.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Clinical <ava@medicore.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLA comparison & proposed failover qualification for MediCore

Rachel —

Appreciate the clear recap. The test slate looks good; a few clarifications from our side before locking windows: 

1) The cross-region failover metric: our internal target for user-facing features is that retries should not add more than 3s median to the 95th percentile. Can you confirm your expected RTO and whether the fallback adds model-switch latency vs. pure routing?

2) For graceful degradation: we need deterministic behavior rather than probabilistic sampling. If you fall back to a smaller model, we want a clear signal in responses (header/metadata) and a way to pin routes to use the fallback permanently for test users.

3) Regarding rate-limits: we have bursty nights that can spike 10x baseline for short windows. Can Redwood guarantee Retry-After headers and consistent 429 bodies for automated retry logic? Also, how are error budgets exposed to us (dashboard and webhook)?

We can open a 3-hour test slot on Thursday 2027-05-13 10:00–13:00 PT. Please confirm the credentials/process for test ingestion so we can whitelist the IPs.

Thanks,
Tom Barton
Head of Platform
MediCore Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tom Barton <tom.barton@medicore.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 01:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLA comparison & proposed failover qualification for MediCore

Tom / Rachel —

Thanks for the clarifications. Short answers and the operational plan below.

1) Cross-region RTO: our internal target for regional failover adds ~1.2s median overhead in the Redwood routing layer when routing to a warm region (kv cache and model already loaded). If the fallback requires model spin-up in a cold region, worst-case observed RTO can reach 6–8s; we will ensure the test includes both warm and cold failover scenarios.

2) Graceful degradation controls: Redwood emits model-version and degrade-mode headers on every response (x-redwood-model-version, x-redwood-degrade-reason). You can pin routes via the Console to force fallback model variants for specific API keys or session tags. We'll include a route pinning step in the PoC plan so you get deterministic behavior.

3) Rate-limits and Retry-After: Redwood returns structured 429 responses with Retry-After and a consistent JSON schema for backoff. We'll publish the rate-limit buckets for the PoC keys and create test keys with elevated burst allowance. Error budgets will be visible in the Console per-route SLI charts and we can send webhook alerts to your incident topic for threshold breaches.

Operational plan for Thu 2027-05-13 10:00–13:00 PT: 
- 09:30 PT: Redwood test account + PoC keys provisioned and IPs whitelisted. (Rachel to share temporary creds)
- 10:00 PT: Ramp 0→600 rps over 10 minutes, hold 45 minutes, then spike to 1200 rps for 5 minutes.
- 11:10 PT: Trigger graceful-degrade by simulating capacity pressure and switch route pins for 5 test tokens.
- 11:40 PT: Cross-region failover warm test: fail primary AZ LB to force routing to warm fallback region.
- 12:10 PT: Cold-start failover: force cold region model spin-up and measure RTO/latency.
- 12:40 PT: Rate-limit mapping run with 50 concurrent clients to induce 429s and verify Retry-After semantics.
- 12:55 PT: KV-cache warm-up window: measure first-request penalty across a 30-minute rolling window.

I've attached a refined PoC plan and the SLA comparison matrix (sheet highlights differences in error-handling and fallback strategies vs MajorCloud). Rachel — can you send the temporary credentials and Drive folder link to the team so Tom can add IP ranges?

Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-poctest-plan.md (updated), redwood-sla-matrix.xlsx (updated)

Ben / team —

Quick note from leadership side to align on commercial/entitlements before we run the test: if MediCore wants explicit SLA credits for cross-region availability and an error-budget contract (rather than standard hosted terms), we should route that through Sales legal. Tom — can you confirm whether you expect a signed addendum or if you prefer to run the qualification first and then formalize (common for pilots)?

If you want an addendum pre-test we can expedite a short pilot agreement (30-day pilot, capped spend, SLA carve-outs) but it will need a countersign from MediCore procurement. Otherwise we will run the qualification under our standard trial terms and capture metrics for a follow-up commercial conversation.

I'll leave the approval to Ben for any temporary elevated burst allowances during the PoC. Rachel — please coordinate the creds and confirm the Drive folder link.

Marcus

Redwood Inference
